title: Ashwani v. Managing Director, Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and 2 Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J. and Kshitij Shailendra, J.
disposition: Bill dispute referred to Executive Engineer under clause 6.5
headnote: On consent, a dispute over the correctness of an electricity bill was referred under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for decision by the concerned Executive Engineer. Respondent no. 2 was directed to decide it, in light of the objection dated 1 January 2024, within six weeks of communication of the order and a photocopy of the objection, and the writ was disposed of.
facts: Ashwani, a consumer, disputed the correctness of an electricity bill issued by Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and approached the Allahabad High Court in Writ-C No. 9298 of 2024. He had already lodged a written objection dated 1 January 2024. The Managing Director and two other officers of the licensee were arrayed as respondents. At the hearing both sides accepted that the bill-correctness dispute should be placed before the concerned Executive Engineer under the Supply Code.

holding_units.topic: referral of a bill-correctness dispute to the Executive Engineer
holding_units.holding: Where counsel agree that a dispute over the correctness of an electricity bill be referred under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for decision by the concerned Executive Engineer, the writ is disposed of by directing respondent no. 2 to decide that dispute, in light of the objection dated 1 January 2024, within six weeks of communication of the order together with a photocopy of the objection.

principle_tags.application: Both sides agreed that the dispute over correctness of the electricity bill be referred under clause 6.5 for decision by the concerned Executive Engineer, and the Court directed respondent no. 2 to decide it.
The objection dated 1 January 2024 was left to be decided within six weeks of communication of the order along with a photocopy of the objection.
The writ was disposed of without adjudicating the bill, the parties having accepted clause 6.5 as the forum for the correctness dispute.

not_decided.point: Whether the electricity bill was correct
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the bill. Decision was left to respondent no. 2 under clause 6.5, in light of the objection dated 1 January 2024.
